title: Global Food Security Reauthorization Act of 2017
official_summary:
Global Food Security Reauthorization Act of 2017

This bill amends the Global Food Security Act of 2016 to: (1) extend through FY2023 the program to carry out those portions of the global food security strategy that relate to the Department of State and the U.S. Agency for International Development, and (2) expand requirements for reporting by the President regarding strategy implementation.

The Foreign Assistance Act of 1961 is amended to extend through FY2023 the assistance program for international disaster relief and rehabilitation, including the set-aside for the emergency food security program.

summary.headline: This law extends U.S. global food security and disaster food aid programs through fiscal year 2023 and adds more reporting requirements for the President.
summary.what_it_does: The law changes the Global Food Security Act of 2016 so that the part of the global food security strategy run by the State Department and USAID continues through fiscal year 2023. It also requires the President to report more information about how that strategy is being carried out. In addition, it amends the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961 to extend the international disaster relief and rehabilitation program through fiscal year 2023, including a set-aside for emergency food security aid.

who_it_affects.group: People in countries receiving U.S. global food security and emergency food aid
who_it_affects.how: Food security and emergency food assistance programs run by State and USAID are authorized to continue through fiscal year 2023.

who_it_affects.group: State Department and USAID staff who run these programs
who_it_affects.how: They must follow expanded reporting requirements on how the global food security strategy is being implemented.
Lawmakers receive more detailed reports from the President on the strategy's progress.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: Enacted October 11, 2018; the program extensions run through fiscal year 2023.
